We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 4 & 1 & -7 & 3 \\  & ↓ & 4 & -12 \\  & 1 & -3 & -9\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-7x+3}{x-4}=x-3-\frac{9}{x-4}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{2}-7x+3}{x-4}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(x-3-\frac{9}{x-4})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x-3{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}x-9{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{x-4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{2}-3x\,{|}_{0}^{2}-9\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-4|\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({2}^{2}-{0}^{2})-3(2-0)-9(\operatorname{ln}⁡|2-4|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0-4|) \\  & =2-6-9(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) \\  & =-4+9(\operatorname{ln}⁡4-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{2})-4 \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2-4.\end{aligned}
$$
